The repo ships a tokens.json with a predictable, publicly known admin token (masked dori…56) that the TokenManager loads by default from the working directory; anyone who enables ENABLE_TOKEN_AUTH without replacing the file accepts a token every reader of the repo knows. It is bound to the Doris root user with an empty password.
fix: Do not ship tokens.json; ship tokens.json.example, refuse to start if a known default token is present, and generate random tokens at setup. Rotate any deployed copy.

reason: decode_token_unsafe is only used by get_token_info, which nothing in the code calls; real JWT validation goes through validate_token with jwt_verify_signature defaulting to True. Not an auth bypass today, but a footgun.

title: get_sql_profile runs the caller's SQL with the security validator skipped (and on the global high-privilege pool)
reason: get_auth_context() reads a ContextVar that nothing ever sets (set_auth_context has no callers; main.py sets the different security.mcp_auth_context_var), so auth_context is None and DorisConnection.execute skips validate_sql_security; calling get_sql_profile with sql='DROP TABLE x' (or any INSERT/DELETE/GRANT) and catalog_name='internal' executes it unchecked. The connection also comes from the global pool (get_connection("query")), so token-bound lower-privilege DB users are bypassed.
fix: Read mcp_auth_context_var (or delete the duplicate ContextVar), make DorisConnection.execute always validate (build a default AuthContext when none is set instead of skipping), allow only SELECT/WITH in get_sql_profile, and use the per-token pool via execute_query.

title: exec_query runs model-written SQL guarded only by a keyword blocklist, as Doris root by default
reason: Arbitrary SQL from the tool argument is executed after a blocklist (DROP/CREATE/ALTER/.../KILL) and regex checks, which the review guide treats as not a working guard; statements outside the list (e.g. SET GLOBAL, ADMIN SET ... CONFIG, SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE / EXPORT to remote storage) are not blocked, and the default DB user is root.
fix: Connect exec_query with a dedicated Doris user that has only SELECT on the intended databases; switch to an allowlist (single SELECT/WITH/SHOW/DESCRIBE statement, parsed) rather than a blocklist; require client approval for this tool.

title: All MCP request headers, including Authorization tokens, are logged at INFO
reason: Every HTTP MCP request writes its raw headers (Authorization bearer token, cookies) to the log, so anyone with log access can replay any client's token.
fix: Remove the header dump or redact authorization/cookie/x-api-key before logging; log at DEBUG at most.

title: HTTP transport runs with no authentication by default (anonymous context gets full tool access)

evidence.quote: enable_token_auth: bool = False  # Enable token-based authentication (default: disabled)
# Return anonymous context when no authentication is enabled

reason: With all auth switches off (the default), every HTTP caller gets an anonymous context and can use exec_query/get_sql_profile against the configured (root by default) Doris connection. Impact depends on whether HTTP mode is used and which host it binds to (docs show --host 0.0.0.0).
fix: Refuse to start the HTTP transport unless an auth method is enabled (or bind to 127.0.0.1 only), and check Origin/Host. User should confirm deployment mode and exposure.
